```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = FALSE,
  comment = "#>"
)
with_dt <- requireNamespace("DT", quietly = TRUE)
rc <- hoopR::return_columns
rc <- rc[order(rc$fn), ]
```

Each row is one column of a data frame a hoopR function returns: the function
(`fn`), the element of the returned list it belongs to (`component`, empty for a
function that returns a single data frame), the column name, its type and what
it holds. Type a function name into the `fn` filter to see everything it
returns, or a column name into `col_name` to find every function that returns
it. The NBA and men's college basketball functions show the same tables in
their help pages; for the other families this table is the column reference.

The same table ships with the package as `hoopR::return_columns`, so in R
`subset(return_columns, fn == "nba_boxscoretraditionalv3")` gives the rows for
one function.

```{r eval = with_dt}
DT::datatable(rc, options = list(scrollX = TRUE, pageLength = 25, deferRender = TRUE), filter = "top", rownames = FALSE)
```

```{r eval = !with_dt}
knitr::kable(rc)
```

To cite the [**`hoopR`**](https://hoopR.sportsdataverse.org/) R package in publications, use:

BibTeX Citation

```bibtex
@misc{hoopr,
  author = {Saiem Gilani},

```
